_doc: MATERIALIZATION IS REPEALED — transcripts/LAYER_STRUCTURE.md §13,
RULED by JYH 2026-07-28.
WHAT THE SHIPPED SPEC SAID, AND WHY IT HAD TO GO. `workspace/panels/
layers.yaml` and `workspace/actions.yaml` §toggle_element_lock both
specified MATERIALIZATION: locking a container SAVED each direct child's
lock state into transient app state, then WROTE `locked = true` onto
every one of them, one level deep, and unlocking restored the saved
values. Meanwhile the Rust comments at controller.rs and
doc_primitives.rs asserted the OPPOSITE — that the lock is not
materialized onto children. The spec and the implementation contradicted
each other IN WRITING, and neither actually protected the contents.
Inheritance and materialization cannot both stand: kept together they
DOUBLE-APPLY, and the children end up carrying flags an artist never set.
WHY THIS FAMILY IS NEW MACHINERY. The lock button's document work lived
only behind a Dioxus click handler and a SwiftUI closure — no op verb, no
action, no gesture reached it — so `toggle_element_lock` was invisible to
every shared corpus in this repository, which is how a spec that
contradicted its own implementation shipped. The `toggle_element_lock` op
verb added with this family routes through the SAME pure function the
panel calls (jas_dioxus `toggle_element_lock_at`, JasSwift
`Document.togglingElementLock`), so it is a gate on the panel's behaviour
and not a second copy of it.
WHAT SURVIVES THE REPEAL, and is pinned here so it cannot be deleted with
the rest: locking an element still PRUNES it and its descendants from the
selection. That is not cosmetic — nothing downstream refuses to move or
delete a selected element for being locked (SCOPE-effective-locked.md
§2), so a lock that left the selection alone would leave locked content
draggable.
WHAT THIS FAMILY CANNOT REACH: the restore-on-unlock BEHAVIOUR being
deleted was keyed off app-lived state in Rust (`layers_saved_lock_states`)
and view-lived `@State` in Swift. Neither is document state, so no golden
here can assert the table is gone — only that unlocking a container
leaves its children exactly as they were. The tables' deletion is watched
by the compiler and by the per-port panel tests.
name: lock_toggle_setup_is_one_layer_of_two_rects

_doc: THE HEADLINE. Locking a LAYER writes the layer's own flag and NOTHING ELSE. Before the repeal both children came back locked:true — flags the artist never set, which then survived into the saved file.
name: locking_a_layer_writes_only_the_layers_own_flag

_doc: Lock then unlock returns the document to exactly where it started. Before the repeal the round trip was LOSSY through this seam: the lock wrote locked:true onto both children and the unlock — with no restore table to consult — left them locked while the layer itself opened.
name: locking_then_unlocking_a_layer_is_a_round_trip

_doc: The same rule for a GROUP, one level down. group_nested.svg is layer -> group -> two rects, so this also proves the repeal is about containers and not about layers specifically.
name: locking_a_group_writes_only_the_groups_own_flag

_doc: A LEAF has no children to materialize onto, so this case is unchanged by the repeal — it is the control that keeps the fix from being 'stop writing the flag at all'.
name: locking_a_leaf_flips_its_own_flag

_doc: STEP 3 SURVIVES: locking an element removes it AND its descendants from the selection. The marquee selects both rects, then the LAYER is locked; the selection must come back empty even though the entries named the children, not the layer.
name: locking_a_layer_prunes_its_descendants_from_the_selection

_doc: UNLOCKING does not prune. The rect is selected, locked (which drops it from the selection), then unlocked — and the selection stays empty, because an unlock speaks to the lock flag and to nothing else.
name: unlocking_a_leaf_does_not_restore_the_selection
